frontmatter.title: Qubitization and quantum signal processing
frontmatter.description: Explicit block encoding, a cosine primitive and postselected complex Hamiltonian evolution.

children.value: A product formula approximates evolution by many short term rotations. Quantum signal processing instead transforms a block encoding of the Hamiltonian into a polynomial in its normalized eigenvalues. Ancilla phase rotations choose the polynomial; repeated accesses apply it to every spectral component without loading eigenvectors. Qubitization supplies the invariant two-dimensional spaces on which that signal-processing picture applies
. It distinguishes the checked cosine-filter primitive, the complex cosine/sine combination, and
. Their normalization and success costs differ.

Actual circuit blocks are compared with independent spectral cosine and matrix-exponential references, while scalar response, coefficient reconstruction and truncation evidence are recorded separately. Additional negative/Y coefficients, complex inputs and nonnormal amplification tests check phase and conditioning behavior. These are bounded numerical checks. No reproduced Lean theorem or certified synthesis sequence is included.
